events.text: First documented; timber castle replaced by stone enclosure castle built or enhanced by Richard Siward.

evidence.quote: Tibbers was first documented in 1298 at which point the timber castle was replaced by a stone castle
It was first recorded in 1298 when Sir Richard Siward , either built the stone enclosure castle or enhanced one
When Richard Siward remodelled the castle it is likely that he added the motte with its stone enclosure castle

events.label: visit
events.text: King Edward I of England visited the castle.

evidence.quote: King Edward I of England visited the castle the same year

events.text: £100 spent on the structure while it was manned by a 23-strong garrison.

evidence.quote: £100 was spent on the structured while it was manned by a 23-strong garrison

events.text: Robert the Bruce's campaign captured the English-held castle.

evidence.quote: The first phase of Bruces campaign in 1306 was to capture the English-held castles of Ayr , Dalswinton , Inverkip and Tibbers

events.text: Scots regained control of the region; castle remained in Scottish hands.

evidence.quote: before returning to Scottish control in 1313
In 1313 the Scots regained control of the region

events.text: Earldom and castle given to Patrick, Earl of March after John Randolph's death at Nevilles Cross.

evidence.quote: in 1346 the earldom along with Tibbers Castle was given to Patrick

events.text: Patrick's son inherited the earldom and acquired the Morton barony.

evidence.quote: His son inherited in 1369 and acquired the barony of Morton

events.text: Dunbar family lands confiscated by the Scottish Crown.

evidence.quote: until 1435 when their lands were confiscated by the Scottish Crown

events.text: King James II of Scotland gave Tibbers to George Crichton, Lord High Admiral.

evidence.quote: In 1450 or 1451 , King James II of Scotland subsequently gave Tibbers to George Crichton

events.label: toun
events.text: A toun or township at Tibbers was mentioned

evidence.quote: A toun or township at Tibbers was mentioned in 1451

events.text: Property returned to royal control after George Crichton's death.

evidence.quote: When he died in 1454 the property again came under royal control

events.label: excavation
events.text: Earliest recorded excavation at the castle; recovered two coins and a dagger.

evidence.quote: The earliest recorded excavation at Tibbers Castle took place in 1864
